cases.sentence: Перед разложенным на столе планом сидели Кутузов и ___ гофкригсрата.
cases.explain: «австрийский член» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: On returning from the review, Kutúzov took the Austrian general into his private room and, calling his adjutant, asked for some papers relating to the condition of the troops on their arrival, and the letters that had come from the Archduke Ferdinand, who was in command of the advanced army. Prince Andréy Bolkónski came into the room with the required papers. Kutúzov and the Austrian member of the Hofkriegsrath were sitting at the table on which a plan was spread out.

cases.sentence: — Я только говорю одно, генерал, — говорил Кутузов с ___ выражений и интонации, заставлявшим вслушиваться в каждое неторопливо-сказанное слово.
cases.explain: «приятным изяществом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “All I can say, General,” said he with a pleasant elegance of expression and intonation that obliged one to listen to each deliberately spoken word. It was evident that Kutúzov himself listened with pleasure to his own voice. “All I can say, General, is that if the matter depended on my personal wishes, the will of His Majesty the Emperor Francis would have been fulfilled long ago. I should long ago have joined the archduke. And believe me on my honour that to me personally it would be a pleasure to hand over the supreme command of the army into the hands of a better informed and more skillful general—of whom Austria has so many—and to lay down all this heavy responsibility. But circumstances are sometimes too strong for us, General.”

cases.sentence: — Я только одно говорю, генерал, что ежели бы дело зависело от моего ___, то воля его величества императора Франца давно была бы исполнена.
cases.explain: «личного желания» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “All I can say, General,” said he with a pleasant elegance of expression and intonation that obliged one to listen to each deliberately spoken word. It was evident that Kutúzov himself listened with pleasure to his own voice. “All I can say, General, is that if the matter depended on my personal wishes, the will of His Majesty the Emperor Francis would have been fulfilled long ago. I should long ago have joined the archduke. And believe me on my honour that to me personally it would be a pleasure to hand over the supreme command of the army into the hands of a better informed and more skillful general—of whom Austria has so many—and to lay down all this heavy responsibility. But circumstances are sometimes too strong for us, General.”

cases.sentence: ___ имел недовольный вид, но не мог не в том же тоне отвечать Кутузову.
cases.explain: «Австрийский генерал» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The Austrian general looked dissatisfied, but had no option but to reply in the same tone.

cases.sentence: Действительно, ___, полученное им из армии Мака, извещало его о победе и о самом выгодном стратегическом положении армии.
cases.explain: «последнее письмо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The general frowned. Though there was no definite news of an Austrian defeat, there were many circumstances confirming the unfavorable rumors that were afloat, and so Kutúzov’s suggestion of an Austrian victory sounded much like irony. But Kutúzov went on blandly smiling with the same expression, which seemed to say that he had a right to suppose so. And, in fact, the last letter he had received from Mack’s army informed him of a victory and stated strategically the position of the army was very favorable.

cases.sentence: — И из всего этого чистенько, на ___, составь memorandum,[252] промеморийку, записочку, для видимости всех тех известий, которые мы о действиях австрийской армии имели.
cases.explain: «французском языке» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Excuse me, General,” interrupted Kutúzov, also turning to Prince Andréy. “Look here, my dear fellow, get from Kozlóvski all the reports from our scouts. Here are two letters from Count Nostitz and here is one from His Highness the Archduke Ferdinand and here are these,” he said, handing him several papers, “make a neat memorandum in French out of all this, showing all the news we have had of the movements of the Austrian army, and then give it to his excellency.”

cases.sentence: Князь Андрей наклонил голову в знак того, что понял с ___ не только то, что̀ было сказано, но и то, что желал бы сказать ему Кутузов.
cases.explain: «первых слов» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy bowed his head in token of having understood from the first not only what had been said but also what Kutúzov would have liked to tell him. He gathered up the papers and with a bow to both, stepped softly over the carpet and went out into the waiting room.

cases.sentence: Он собрал бумаги, и, отдав ___, тихо шагая по ковру, вышел в приемную.
cases.explain: «общий поклон» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy bowed his head in token of having understood from the first not only what had been said but also what Kutúzov would have liked to tell him. He gathered up the papers and with a bow to both, stepped softly over the carpet and went out into the waiting room.

cases.sentence: Кутузов, которого он догнал еще в Польше, принял его очень ласково, обещал ему не забывать его, отличал от ___, брал с собою в Вену и давал более серьезные поручения.
cases.explain: «других адъютантов» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Kutúzov, whom he had overtaken in Poland, had received him very kindly, promised not to forget him, distinguished him above the other adjutants, and had taken him to Vienna and given him the more serious commissions. From Vienna Kutúzov wrote to his old comrade, Prince Andréy’s father.

cases.sentence: Из Вены Кутузов писал своему ___, отцу князя Андрея:
cases.explain: «старому товарищу» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Kutúzov, whom he had overtaken in Poland, had received him very kindly, promised not to forget him, distinguished him above the other adjutants, and had taken him to Vienna and given him the more serious commissions. From Vienna Kutúzov wrote to his old comrade, Prince Andréy’s father.
